criteria.text: The participant has a histologically or cytologically confirmed metastatic or unresectable solid malignancy within one of the listed tumor types.
The participant has non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC).
The participant has head and neck squamous cell cancer (HNSCC).
The participant has advanced HER2-negative breast cancer.
The participant has esophageal squamous cell carcinoma (ESCC).
The participant has esophageal/gastro-esophageal junction adenocarcinoma (EAC/GEJ).
The participant has cutaneous squamous cell cancer (cSCC).
The participant has exocrine pancreatic adenocarcinoma.
The participant has bladder cancer.
The participant has cervical cancer.
The participant has gastric cancer.
The participant has high grade serous ovarian cancer (HGSOC).
In Part A, the participant has disease that is relapsed or refractory or is intolerant to standard-of-care therapies and has no appropriate standard-of-care therapeutic options.

In Part B, the participant has disease that is relapsed or refractory or is intolerant to standard-of-care therapies. The participant has received platinum-based therapy and a PD-1/PD-(L)1 inhibitor, if applicable and available.

In Part C, for pembrolizumab combination cohorts, the participant is eligible for pembrolizumab per local standard of care. For pembrolizumab with cisplatin or carboplatin, the participant is eligible for both pembrolizumab and the platinum agent per local standard of care. The participant is treatment naïve for locally advanced or metastatic systemic therapy (prior definitively intended or [neo]adjuvant therapy is allowed).
In Part D, the participant is treatment naïve for locally advanced or metastatic systemic therapy.
The participant has a tumor site accessible for biopsy and agrees to biopsy.
In Part B and Part D, a baseline fresh tumor biopsy is required. An archival biopsy collected within 90 days prior to first dose of study drug may be used.
In the Biology expansion cohort, a pretreatment biopsy and on-treatment (Cycle 1) biopsy are required.
The participant has an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) Performance Status of 0 or 1.
The participant has measurable disease per the RECIST v1.1 at baseline.

The participant has a history of another malignancy within 3 years before first dose of study drug, or any evidence of residual disease from a previously diagnosed malignancy. Exceptions are malignancies with a negligible risk of metastasis or death.
The participant has known active central nervous system metastases. Participants with previously treated brain metastases may participate provided they:
The participant is clinically stable for at least 4 weeks prior to study entry after brain metastasis treatment.
The participant has no new or enlarging brain metastases.
The participant is off of corticosteroids prescribed for symptoms associated with brain metastases for at least 7 days prior to first dose of study drug.

In Part D, the participant has untreated, asymptomatic CNS metastases smaller than 1 cm and may be enrolled without definitive treatment as long as they have no neurological symptoms, no or minimal surrounding edema, and no requirements for corticosteroids.
The participant has carcinomatous meningitis.
The participant has previously received an MMAE-containing agent or an agent targeting integrin beta-6.

The participant has pre-existing neuropathy Grade 1 or greater per the National Cancer Institute's Common Terminology Criteria for Adverse Events, version 5.0 (NCI CTCAE v5.0) for Parts C and D cohorts with cisplatin or carboplatin; Grade 2 or greater per the NCI CTCAE v5.0 for all other cohorts.
The participant has any uncontrolled Grade 3 or higher (per NCI CTCAE v5.0) viral, bacterial, or fungal infection within 2 weeks prior to the first dose of sigvotatug vedotin.
Routine antimicrobial prophylaxis is permitted.

The participant has Grade ≥3 pulmonary disease unrelated to underlying malignancy. This includes clinically severe pulmonary function compromise resulting from clinically significant pulmonary illnesses.

In Part C and D, the participant has prior therapy with a PD-1 inhibitor, anti-PD-(L)1, or anti PD-L2 agent or with an agent directed to another stimulatory or co-inhibitory T-cell receptor and was discontinued from that treatment due to a Grade 3 or higher immune-mediated adverse event (IMAE).

The participant has a history of noninfectious interstitial lung disease (ILD) or pneumonitis that required steroids, current ILD or pneumonitis, or suspected ILD or pneumonitis that cannot be ruled out by imaging at screening.
The participant has a known diffusing capacity of the lung for carbon monoxide (DLCO; adjusted for hemoglobin) <50% predicted.

The participant is investigator site staff directly involved in the conduct of the study and their family members, site staff otherwise supervised by the investigator, and sponsor and sponsor delegate employees directly involved in the conduct of the study and their family members.

transcript.text: These questions are about the trial "A Study of Sigvotatug Vedotin in Advanced Solid Tumors". Your earlier answers already covered 7 of its rules. I'll ask about the rest of its rules one at a time. You can skip any question, and "I don't know" is always fine.

transcript.text: Thanks. For your lung cancer, have you tried all standard treatment options that are usually available, or are you out of options?

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. In the 2 weeks before starting the study, have you had any serious infections like pneumonia, sepsis, or a severe fungal infection that required hospitalization or strong IV antibiotics?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't had any serious infections like that. I have HIV, but it's undetectable on my meds for years.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Do you have any lung or breathing conditions (like COPD or severe asthma) that are not related to your cancer?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I don't have COPD or severe asthma. Just the lung cancer.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Have you ever stopped treatment with a PD-1, PD-L1, or PD-L2 inhibitor (or similar immune-boosting cancer therapy) because of a severe side effect (Grade 3 or higher) related to your immune system?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I haven't. I haven't had any immunotherapy like PD-1 inhibitors yet, so I couldn't have stopped one due to side effects.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thanks. Are you currently working for the study site or the sponsor company, or are you a family member of someone who works directly on this study?

transcript.speaker: participant
transcript.text: No, I'm not. I'm just an accountant with lung cancer looking for a trial.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.text: Thank you, that's all my questions. Your record for this trial is ready, for you and your oncologist. They and the trial team decide whether it is right for you.
